subtitle: Set usage limits and access tiers for this location.
blockedMovedPrefix: Looking for blocked guests? They are now under
limitsApplyNote: A speed change reaches guests who are already online, usually within a minute. Timeouts and device count apply the next time each guest connects — anyone online right now keeps those until then. A data limit is different: it counts usage guests have already spent this period, so adding or lowering one can sign someone out within minutes.

venueSpeed.label: Total venue speed
venueSpeed.caption: The most all guests together can use at this venue.
venueSpeed.unavailable: Not available on this venue's hardware.
venueSpeed.errorBelowPerGuest: Must be at least the per-guest speed ({{perGuest}}).
venueSpeed.errorRange: Must be between 1 Mbps and 10,000 Mbps.
venueSpeed.notSaved: Limits saved for {{location}}, but the total venue speed was not — it reads back as {{actual}}.
venueSpeed.unavailableAruba: Wyfy can't set a total for the whole venue at Aruba Instant On venues yet. A network-wide limit applies to one guest network, not the whole venue, and a network uses either that or the per-device speed, not both.

guestSpeed.applyUnreachable: We couldn't reach Instant On to change the speed, so nothing has changed.
guestSpeed.title: Guest speed limit (per device)
guestSpeed.readFailed: We couldn't read the guest WiFi speed from Instant On just now. Reload to try again.
guestSpeed.noNetwork: Instant On shows no guest WiFi network at this venue yet.
guestSpeed.confirmTitle: Change the speed for every guest device?
guestSpeed.confirmBody: Every device on {{network}} will be held to {{down}} down and {{up}} up. We'll confirm with Instant On before saying it's done.
guestSpeed.sameForEveryDevice: One speed for every device on this guest WiFi network. Aruba Instant On can't give one guest a different speed from another, so this applies to everyone on it alike. It's the most a device can use, not a guaranteed speed.
guestSpeed.sameSettingAsTiers: Speed tiers by WiFi network (below) set this same Instant On speed for their networks: whichever is applied last is the one Instant On holds.
guestSpeed.needsCloud: Setting the guest WiFi speed from Wyfy needs Instant On cloud control, which isn't switched on for this venue yet. Ask your Wyfy Guest contact to turn it on.

limitsTable.subtitle: What guests get at each location. A location marked Default has nothing saved yet.
limitsTable.defaultHint: Nothing has been saved for this location yet, so its guests get these defaults.
limitsTable.loadFailedBody: Reload the page to try again. Saving is paused until they load, so nothing is duplicated.
limitsTable.saveBlocked: Could not read the saved limits, so nothing was saved. Reload and try again.

ssidGuests.title: Guests who can use {{ssid}}
ssidGuests.hint: Add a guest here and they can join this network without a voucher, from their next connection. Removing them stops the next connection, not one already online.
ssidGuests.loadFailed: Couldn't load this network's guest list.
ssidGuests.searchLabel: Find a guest by phone or email
ssidGuests.noResults: No guest found at this location. A guest appears here after signing in once.

networkTotal.explain: One total shared by all devices on this WiFi network. It's per network, not for the whole venue. A network has either a per-device limit or a total, so this replaces any per-device limit.
networkTotal.previewClear: This removes the total from this network. Guests on it will have no speed limit.
networkTotal.preview: All devices on this network will share {{down}} down and {{up}} up.
networkTotal.applied: Instant On confirmed the new network total.
networkTotal.notChanged: Instant On didn't change the speed. Reason: {{reason}}
networkTotal.restored: Instant On didn't keep the network total. The previous setting was put back.
networkTotal.stateUnknown: Instant On didn't confirm the network total, and we don't know what's set now. Reload this page to read it again.
networkTotal.noAnswer: We didn't get an answer, so we don't know whether this changed. Reload this page to see what's set now.

ssidTiers.title: Speed tiers by WiFi network
ssidTiers.intro: Run a free and a paid guest network side by side. Guests with a voucher, or on the network's guest list, can join the paid network; everyone else stays on the free one.
ssidTiers.oneSpeed: Each WiFi network has one speed for all its guests. Aruba Instant On can't give one guest a different speed from another on the same network.
ssidTiers.paidHint: Guests without a voucher who aren't on this network's guest list are turned away from this network and shown how to get a voucher.
ssidTiers.saved: Saved. Wyfy now checks who may join each network when a guest signs in. Each network's speed is applied once cloud control is on for this venue; until then it is saved here only.
ssidTiers.loadFailed: Couldn't load the WiFi networks for this location.
ssidTiers.empty: No networks mapped. Every guest on every WiFi network is treated the same.
ssidTiers.openToAll: Open to every guest who signs in.
ssidTiers.rowSpeed: Speed: {{speed}}, the same for every guest on “{{ssid}}”.
ssidTiers.speedsAppliedBody: Speeds are applied to the access points once cloud control is on for this venue. Until then they are saved here only.

speed.allApplied: Every mapped network's speed is applied on the access points.
speed.awaitingSetup: Speeds are applied to the access points once cloud control is on for this venue. Until then they are saved here only.
speed.notYetApplied: Saved here, not applied to the access points yet.
speed.notAllApplied: Some networks' speeds aren't applied to the access points yet.
speed.applyFailed: The last attempt to apply this speed didn't go through.
speed.networkNotFound: No guest WiFi network with this name was found at this venue.
speed.networkHasOtherLimit: This network has a network-wide limit that wasn't set from Wyfy, so Wyfy leaves it as it is.
speed.confirm: Apply these speeds to the guest WiFi now? Guests on each network get its new speed.
speed.appliedToast: Speeds applied to every mapped network.
speed.noAnswerToast: We didn't get an answer, so we don't know whether the speeds changed. Reload this page to see what's set now.

nasOnly.dataLimit: Usage is counted. When a guest reaches the limit they can't sign in again, but Wyfy can't disconnect a device from Aruba Instant On access points, so they stay online until their session ends.
nasOnly.dataLimitCloud: Usage is counted. When a guest reaches the limit, Wyfy takes their device off the WiFi through Instant On, within about 5 minutes of crossing it (usage arrives every ~5 minutes), and they can't sign in again until the limit resets. If Instant On doesn't confirm the block, the guest is refused at their next sign-in instead.
nasOnly.idleTimeout: Your access points may not apply this; sessions still end at the session timeout.
nasOnly.dailyLimit: Enforced. When a guest's time for today runs out, Aruba Instant On access points end their session, and they can't sign in again until the allowance resets.
nasOnly.openHours: Enforced at Aruba Instant On access points too: a guest who is online at closing time is signed out then, and nobody can sign in until you open again.
nasOnly.allowList: These rules apply when a guest signs in. Wyfy can't disconnect a device from Aruba Instant On access points, so removing someone, or switching on "only people on this list", doesn't take anyone offline who is online right now. They stay on until their session ends.
nasOnly.allowListCloud: These rules apply when a guest signs in. With "only people on this list" switched on, anyone online who isn't on the list can be taken off the WiFi through Instant On within minutes. Otherwise, removing someone doesn't take them offline until their session ends.
nasOnly.trustedDevices: At Aruba Instant On access points a trusted device still opens the WiFi sign-in page for a moment, then connects on its own, with no code. Removing a device takes effect when its current session ends.
nasOnly.limitsFooter: Changes apply the next time each guest signs in. Aruba Instant On access points end each session when its time is up, so anyone online right now keeps the limits they signed in with until then.
nasOnly.limitsFooterCloud: Time limits and device count apply the next time each guest signs in: Aruba Instant On access points end each session when its time is up, so anyone online right now keeps the time they signed in with until then. A data limit is different: it counts usage guests have already spent, so adding or lowering one can take someone offline within minutes.
